expectations.evidence: Four-zone model (Edge DMZ, App DMZ, Internal, Data) with detailed Neutron network mappings, subnet CIDRs, and VLAN assignments in Section 2.
ModSecurity v3 recommended explicitly with OWASP CRS v4, including specific rule groups (942xxx for SQLi), paranoia level config, and tuning process in Section 3.2.
Apache APISIX with limit-req plugin (rate limiting), jwt-auth plugin (auth), and request-validation plugin (body schema validation) shown in Section 4.3 route configs.
Section 6.1 details TLS termination at HAProxy then re-encryption at every hop: HAProxy->WAF, WAF->APISIX, APISIX->pods via Linkerd mTLS, backend->PostgreSQL with TLS 1.3 verify-full.

HAProxy stick-table rate limiting, conn_rate/http_req_rate thresholds, SYN cookies, nftables, fail2ban, slowloris protection (timeout http-request 5s), and a full DDoS response runbook in Sections 3.1 and 9.2.

expectations.evidence: Cisco ACI contracts with explicit EPG-to-EPG rules (Section 2.3), no contract between edge/app and data zones, plus Calico network policies with default-deny-all per namespace (Section 5.2). Two independent enforcement layers.
APISIX as ingress in K8s (Section 4.2), Calico CNI with default-deny NetworkPolicies (Section 5.2), and Linkerd service mesh with mTLS and ServerAuthorization policies (Section 5.3).
Suricata deployed on Edge DMZ hosts in IDS mode with ET Open ruleset and custom healthcare ePHI exfiltration rules (Section 8.3), plus Wazuh as host IDS and Falco for runtime security.

Centralized logging to Loki with 6-year HIPAA retention (Section 8.4), Wazuh for host-level correlation, all components (HAProxy, ModSecurity, APISIX, Linkerd, pgAudit, Falco, auditd) shipping logs. Grafana dashboards with PagerDuty alerting. Note: no dedicated SIEM product (e.g., Wazuh SIEM or ELK) is named as the SIEM; Loki+Wazuh+Grafana serve that role.

Beyond ModSecurity WAF: parameterized queries enforced via semgrep CI checks, PgBouncer connection pooling, pg_hba.conf client cert auth, pgAudit logging, network isolation preventing direct DB access from DMZ zones (Sections 7.1-7.2).

Section 10 maps HIPAA requirements (164.312 a/b/c/e) to specific implementations. 6-year audit log retention, breach notification runbooks (Section 9.3), ePHI-specific Suricata rules, and encryption at rest/in-transit controls.

Section 12 lists 20 specific FLOSS products with versions and licenses: HAProxy, ModSecurity, OWASP CRS, APISIX, Calico, Linkerd, Suricata, Wazuh, Falco, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PgBouncer, pgAudit, pgBackRest, fail2ban, nftables, cert-manager, OpenBao, keepalived.
